title: False New Year: Doctrine Slayer - True Past Curses & Trauma

sense.text:
Israel were the gifts. “And they that dwell upon the earth shall rejoice over them, and make merry, and shall send gifts one to another”: we were the ones they sent one to another, handed down from one generation of slaveholders to the next. A slaveholder in Granville County, North Carolina gave his son a negro girl named Nutty, about five years old, for the love he bore his son and one cent, to him and his heirs forever. Many of our ancestors were sold as children like that, or given as gifts, passed lovingly from one generation of slaveholders to the next. Merry Christmas.

“Because these two prophets tormented them that dwelt on the earth”: the two prophets are Judah and Ephraim. We were giving them hell when we were ruling, so when we were given into their hands they counted it payback and rejoiced over us.

The paintings of Europe show us being given into their hands: in Britain, Italy, France and Russia, little black boys and girls holding the umbrella over their masters, holding the mirror up so she can look at her pale skin, holding the bird, the horse, the dog and the music, serving apples at the table. A grown sister in Nantes, a heavy slave-trade port in France, still has the yoke on her neck; she was brought there as a child. These were children stripped from their parents. They called us their favorites: the Princess de Conti of France and her negro favorite, Marie de Bourbon with her negro favorite, a countess in Russia with hers. Lucrezia Borgia, sister of Cesare Borgia and daughter of Pope Alexander VI, is painted with her black favorite: the Borgias owned black slaves and posed as Mary and Christ. The same was done in Japan and China, where the Arabs brought us as slaves, holding the umbrellas over them dressed the exact same way. Today it is the same: Hollywood women adopting feminized black favorites. We lost the war, and it was given unto him to make war with us; we are casualties of war.

“Thy sons and thy daughters shall be given unto another people, and thine eyes shall look, and fail with longing for them all the day long: and there shall be no might in thine hand.” Our children were taken and given into the hands of other people, and we had no power to get them back.

New World Jewry tells how it was done to us under the Inquisition. Thomas Mendes, born in Portugal, went to Luanda in Angola, a Portuguese colony, and knew the locations of all the Jewish communities in Europe, Africa and the New World; he and his wife were convicted in Veracruz in 1647 of observing the law of Moses, she given a hundred lashes and he two hundred, both sentenced to perpetual prison. After the autos-da-fé, the public burnings, hundreds of innocent women and children were devastated. We were closely knit families, where love and affection were showered on the children, and the children became wards of the Holy Office, the Catholic Church, given to foster parents who had to feed them, clothe them, indoctrinate them with Catholic dogmas, and teach them to abhor anything Jewish and despise all Jews. They were taught that the Jews killed our Lord and were cursed to perpetual wandering. That is the same doctrine the Christians still preach: you Israelites killed Christ, the Jews rejected him and are cast away. They taught us to hate ourselves with Christianity.

When the Jews were expelled, they were given eight months to leave. Those who could not pay to get out were deemed illegal immigrants, caught and sold as slaves, just like Trump is doing now. Young children between three and ten, especially those whose parents had been sold as slaves, were deported to the island of St. Thomas off the coast of Africa and reared as Catholics. The bereaved parents fell flat on their faces before the king on a Sunday as he was leaving church, begging him to withdraw the decree, and he had them dragged from his path and mocked them for crying over their children. It is the same thing as in Roots, when she fell on her knees and begged: hundreds of years before, we were already falling before the king.

Jews and Moors in Spain tells it again. Nearly 150,000 fled Spain into Portugal, and King John II let them stay eight months for a tax, because they were lucrative: armourers and miners. His clemency was short. The plague broke out, the black plague, called black because they blamed the black Jews for it, and the church lashed the people into fury. Then all Jewish children below fourteen were torn from their parents' arms, dragged into the church and baptized. Those under three were given to Christian women to receive a Christian education, in other words to be raised as slaves: their negro favorites. So a Christian education is a doctrine of slavery. If you are Baptist, Pentecostal, Methodist, Seventh-day Adventist or Jehovah's Witness, you were raised as a slave. Those between three and ten were shipped to St. Thomas, the isle of the lost, colonized by condemned criminals, and terrible things were done to us there. Those between ten and fourteen were sold as slaves. Mothers begged to be taken with their babies, were thrust aside, ran behind the ships and drowned in the waves. Then the parents were given the choice between baptism and slavery, and baptism means taking on the Catholic doctrine and a Christian name, the way Kunta became Toby. John II was struck sick the very day the ships of exiled children set sail, and died in 1495. God is good.

So the curse of 28:32 and 41 followed us: we ran from Spain to Portugal, and it followed us into Portugal and into Africa. Our people are still on St. Thomas and in Cape Verde today, mixed in with the white folks.

precepts.why:
“Thou shalt beget sons and daughters, but thou shalt not enjoy them; for they shall go into captivity.” It is the same thing said twice: our sons and daughters would be given into the hands of other people.

The Critical Review lays out who did it. The Arabs were selling us first, from the 700s, before the Portuguese and Spanish; the first rivals of the Arabs in the slaving trade were the Portuguese, from 1445. Their kidnapping was favoured by the Pope: Nicholas V, in his bull Dum Diversas, granted the unknown world to the Portuguese and Spaniards and ordered the Christians to reduce all infidels to slavery. That is the St. Nicholas you worship at Christmas. The trade ran from 1443, long before 1619, through the Portuguese, the English, the Dutch, the French, the Swedes, the Danes, the Prussians and the North Americans. Prince Henry's Guinea company traded with the Arabs, and seven or eight hundred negro slaves a year went to Lisbon by 1455. John II expelled the Jews to St. Thomas and to the Portuguese settlements in Africa, and from these banished Jews came the black Portuguese, as they were called, and the Jews in Loango. The Jews were black people: the Jews of Loango, the black Portuguese and the negroes are the same people, and these negroes were purchased in Guinea and Congo. The Spaniards treated the natives of the West Indies the same way the Pope instructed: enslave the infidel, make him Catholic, change his name. The Native Americans were treated as the Moors and Jews were in Spain, because they are the same people.

Before the Mayflower says the first generation of African Americans entered America with Spanish names, for reasons Lerone Bennett did not know. We know: Antonio, which became Anthony, Maria, Pedro, Francisco, Angola, Tony Congo. They came from Spain, and they were Jews. The foundational black Americans were Jews from Spain and Portugal. J. A. Rogers says negro slavery on a large scale came to Portugal from 1440; the Jews brought in much negro strain; some of the noblest Sephardic families were negroes; a noble family was named Negro, and preto is still the word in Portugal. Negroes were imported into Spain and Portugal in droves from 1440 to 1773, from Senegal, Guinea and Congo, cutting sugar cane in Andalusia before America was discovered. Columbus was plundering negro slaves in Guinea before he stole Indian slaves in Cuba. The negro came to the Indies from Spain, not from Africa, and the mulatto was not made in America: the Moors ruled Spain and Portugal and had children by white women, black fathers and white mothers. That light skin some of you brag about came from a white mother and a black father, so you are still Israelites. We ran from the white man into the hands of the Arabs, and out of the hands of the Arabs into the hands of the white man. The curses follow you wherever you go.

A book from 1850 says the Jews, according to the prophecy, dwelt alone without intermixing with the nations: a separate race, not a religion, all descended from brown ancestors. Abraham, Isaac and Jacob must have been as dark as the Arabs, if not darker, and the Jews show every shade from black to light brown. The Spanish Jew is always dark complexioned with black, curly hair, while the German Jew is as fair as any German, with light or red hair and blue eyes. And the American negroes came from the coast of Guinea. Guinea, Congo, Angola: the same places over and over again.

sense.text: Joseph was one of the twelve sons of Jacob. His brothers hated him and sold him into slavery, and he gained status in Egypt. Through his counsel Egypt survived the famine, so now his brothers come to Egypt to buy food, and “bowed down themselves before him with their faces to the earth.”
He recognized them “but made himself strange unto them, and spake roughly unto them”: he acted as if he did not know them and spoke hard to them. “Whence come ye?” Where are you from?

“And Joseph knew his brethren, but they knew not him.” If Joseph were a German Jew or from Holland, Ukraine or Poland, they would have known him straight away: a white man in Egyptian clothes among black Egyptians stands out. You are not going to confuse Eminem with Ludacris. They could not recognize their own brother because he was dressed in Egyptian garb, beard shaved, made up like an Egyptian, and he looked like one. Joseph passed for an Egyptian, a black man, just like Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, our dark-complexioned ancestors.

They are going through something, and they say among themselves that if it were not for the evil they did to Joseph they would not be going through this: “We are verily guilty concerning our brother.” Reuben says, I warned you: “Spake I not unto you, saying, Do not sin against the child; and ye would not hear?”

“And they knew not that Joseph understood them; for he spake unto them by an interpreter.” They spoke Hebrew in front of him and he understood every word they said about him, but he spoke Egyptian to them through an interpreter, so as not to speak to them directly. He was a good actor: he spoke like an Egyptian, dressed like one and looked like one.

precepts.why:
Joseph sits down to eat, and “they set on for him by himself, and for them by themselves, and for the Egyptians, which did eat with him, by themselves: because the Egyptians might not eat bread with the Hebrews; for that is an abomination unto the Egyptians.” That is Jim Crow. Israel had its own land, Goshen, over here, and Egypt over there, and it was still segregation, despite all of that. Yet Joseph sat as an Egyptian and his brothers did not know him.

The pictures in the books bear it out. The Egyptians are painted brown. Our people work in the granary under a taskmaster with a stick, with afros, black people, and captives are bound by the neck with yokes: we did not just give in, we fought and we lost. Pharaoh is black, and his servants hold the umbrella over him. Tutankhamun, a child king born deformed of a brother and sister, is brown. A synagogue mosaic at Beth Alpha from the sixth century shows Abraham about to sacrifice Isaac, with the ram caught in the thicket, and they are drawn black. Our Living Bible shows the sons of Ham, the Egyptians, Canaanites, Nubians and Libyans, and the Philistine, all dark: same colour, different nations. We fought the Canaanites in the land, conquered them and forced them into West Africa, where they enslaved us with the help of the Arabs. The Semites coming into Egypt have afros and beards too. Joseph passed for one of these.

sense.text: Who else passed for an Egyptian? Moses. “Now there arose up a new king over Egypt, which knew not Joseph.” He saw that “the people of the children of Israel are more and mightier than we”, and said “let us deal wisely with them; lest they multiply”: let us conspire secretly against them, so they do not grow, and so that in a war they do not join our enemies and get up out of the land.

“They did set over them taskmasters to afflict them with their burdens.” “But the more they afflicted them, the more they multiplied and grew.” They made us “serve with rigour”, our lives “bitter with hard bondage, in morter, and in brick, and in all manner of service in the field”: harsh and severe, beating us and whipping us, the same as you saw earlier.

Pharaoh told the Hebrew midwives, Shiphrah and Puah, “if it be a son, then ye shall kill him: but if it be a daughter, then she shall live.” Kill the males, because the nation comes from the man. Keep the women, because they can lie with them and make their own: a woman reproduces what the man provides.

“But the midwives feared God, and did not as the king of Egypt commanded them, but saved the men children alive.” These sisters loved their people and would not let Pharaoh annihilate their race, unlike some sisters today.

The midwives answered Pharaoh that the Hebrew women “are lively, and are delivered ere the midwives come in unto them.” “Therefore God dealt well with the midwives: and the people multiplied, and waxed very mighty.” And because they feared God, “he made them houses”: we built the sisters big houses to thank them for saving our babies.

“Every son that is born ye shall cast into the river, and every daughter ye shall save alive.” That is gator bait. They sacrificed our sons to Sobek, the crocodile god. The white man did the exact same thing in the Florida Everglades: put our babies out in a net to draw the alligator, pull the gator out and make shoes and bags of him. Egypt did it to us first. Kill the males, keep the women, because the women do not produce the nation; the man does.

“There went a man of the house of Levi, and took to wife a daughter of Levi.” She bore a son, “a goodly child”, hid him three months, and when she could hide him no longer she made “an ark of bulrushes” and “laid it in the flags by the river’s brink.”

Pharaoh's daughter opened the ark, “the babe wept”, and she said, “This is one of the Hebrews’ children.” How did she know? He was circumcised. You do not read of Moses being circumcised in Exodus; it was already done, because some of our forefathers retained those customs from our fathers. Outside of that she would not have known the difference, because Egyptian and Hebrew were both black.

His sister offered to call “a nurse of the Hebrew women”, and she called the child's own mother, and Pharaoh's daughter paid her wages to nurse him. The Disney cartoon, the Prince of Egypt, put fiction in it, as if his mother cast him away. No: Moses went back to his mother, she nursed him and got paid for it, all done in secret because the decree to kill the males was still going forth.
She brought him to Pharaoh's daughter, “he became her son”, and she named him Moses, “Because I drew him out of the water.”

Grown, Moses went out to his brethren, “and looked on their burdens: and he spied an Egyptian smiting an Hebrew, one of his brethren.” He looked this way and that, “he slew the Egyptian, and hid him in the sand.”
Pharaoh “sought to slay Moses. But Moses fled from the face of Pharaoh”: now he is a fugitive, and he “dwelt in the land of Midian”.

The shepherds drove away the seven daughters of the priest of Midian, Moses stood up and watered their flock, and they told their father, “An Egyptian delivered us out of the hand of the shepherds”. What did they call Moses? An Egyptian. The same way Joseph's brothers took him for an Egyptian.
The man was Jethro. He was a priest of Midian, not a Midianite. “Call him, that he may eat bread.” And “he gave Moses Zipporah his daughter.”

precepts.why:
What was Jethro? “Miriam and Aaron spake against Moses because of the Ethiopian woman whom he had married: for he had married an Ethiopian woman.” Zipporah was an Ethiopian, so Moses' father-in-law was an Ethiopian, and the Ethiopians are children of Ham.

A Hamite would know a Hamite when he saw one. If Moses were a white man, a Cushite family that knew the Egyptians as kin would have known he was no Egyptian. Yet they called him an Egyptian. Moses passed for an Egyptian the same way Joseph passed for an Egyptian. These are black people. That is the point.

sense.text: “Her Nazarites were purer than snow, they were whiter than milk”: the Nazarites are the Israelites, and whiter here means holier, righteous. “More ruddy in body than rubies” means healthy in body, precious, and “their polishing was of sapphire”: strong. Verse 7 is the before: healthy, well polished and strong.

Then Babylon came, cut off our food supply and starved us out, and verse 8 is the after. “Their visage is blacker than a coal”: their faces. “They are not known in the streets”: you cannot recognize them from verse 7. “Their skin cleaveth to their bones; it is withered, it is become like a stick”: from ruddy in body to skin hanging off their bones, anorexic.

Why blacker than a coal? When black folks are starved there is hyperpigmentation: they get darker. When white folks are starved they get paler, pinker than a pig, not blacker than a coal. Even plants have their melanin, chlorophyll, which gives them their green; deprive a plant of water and sunlight and it turns brown and withers, like the Jews here. That is hyperpigmentation through starvation. They were starved and got darker than they already were.

precepts.why:
“Our skin was black like an oven because of the terrible famine.” What caused the famine? The Babylonians surrounded us, besieged us, cut off our food and water and starved us for years before conquering us entirely, and through starvation we got darker, blacker than a coal. Our skin was black: is that symbolic too? Is your skin a symbol? Black like an oven, and ovens are black. That makes it worse.

It is sad that we have to go through the scientific method of how skin darkens in famine, while all the white man has to say is that he is white, with no science, no archaeology, no scripture, and the people say praise Jesus. We present scriptures, records from the 1600s, history and science, and they still will not accept it. That is white makes right: who is like unto the beast? Even the machine backs it: severe malnutrition and famine can darken and shrivel the skin to a grey or black appearance, and in white people it makes the skin paler, from anemia. Look at the starved Jews of the Holocaust: no dark Anne Frank, no hyperpigmentation, just starved out. Look at our people starving in Ethiopia: darker than a coal, swollen belly, ribs touching. That is the Nazarites after Babylon. That is how we looked when Babylon besieged us.

sense.text: The chief captain asked Paul, “Canst thou speak Greek? Art not thou that Egyptian, which before these days madest an uproar, and leddest out into the wilderness four thousand men that were murderers?” He took him for a particular Egyptian.

“But Paul said, I am a man which am a Jew of Tarsus, a city in Cilicia, a citizen of no mean city”: I am a Jew, and I am not from a bad place. Paul passed for an Egyptian. Moses passed for an Egyptian. Joseph passed for an Egyptian. And Christ too: his family ran into Africa from white folks. What more do you possibly need?

“Judah mourneth, and the gates thereof languish; they are black unto the ground; and the cry of Jerusalem is gone up.” Jeremiah, who wrote Lamentations, is speaking of the same thing: Babylon overthrew us and starved us, and we became black unto the ground. It was saved for last on purpose, because some read it and say it only means mourning, it is symbolic. Simple, unfaithful and weak.

Yes, it speaks of their condition; but there is a reason God put it there. When they call us black people today they are talking about our condition, the lowest people on this earth, beneath the Chinese and the Arabs; but they are also talking about our skin. No Christian can confound us with that.

The dangerous part is brothers who know Israel was black but pull Jeremiah 14:2 and say the elders broke these verses down wrong. When any leader starts hunting for faults in the Bible, fifty scriptures we broke down wrong, that is a sign of unbelief; you should be looking for more commandments to keep. It is one step from teaching Christianity. It is fear: they are adapting, taking up Edomite talking points to separate themselves from the radicals. Either Satan got them or the money did. All these books suddenly appearing that the elders did not write, with a misspelled name, the wrong picture, no ISBN number: it smells like the FBI and CIA, the way J. Edgar Hoover put out propaganda to split the Panthers from the gangs.

“I will also gather all nations, and will bring them down into the valley of Jehoshaphat”: the valley of decision, Armageddon, the coming world war. He will plead with them “for my heritage Israel, whom they have scattered among the nations, and parted my land.” Our land is parted between the Israelis and the Arabs: the same people who were involved in our enslavement.

“They have cast lots for my people”: selling us on the auction block, sold to Sir Charles of Virginia, sold to Ahmed, sold to Hernandez, as you saw in Roots. “And have given a boy for an harlot”: made us breeders, breeding plantations. “And sold a girl for wine, that they might drink.”

“What have ye to do with me, O Tyre, and Zidon, and all the coasts of Palestine?” Tyre is the city; Zidon is the people, the Sidonians, and the Sidonians are Canaanites. When Joshua conquered the Hamites in our land we pushed them into the interior of Africa, and they migrated to the western regions. So when we fled from the white man out of Spain, we ran into them, or into the Arabs. God is saying, what have you to do with me, you Canaanites? You are not my chosen people. The coasts of Palestine are the Arabs, the Palestinians. God did not choose Canaan and he did not choose Ishmael, and these two got together and conquered us. “Swiftly and speedily will I return your recompence upon your own head”.

“Ye have taken my silver and my gold, and have carried into your temples my goodly pleasant things”. Some now say this is not the slave trade but the temple. When did Tyre and Zidon or the coasts of Palestine ever overthrow the temple and carry its things into theirs? Never. Hiram king of Tyre, whose mother was of the northern kingdom and whose father was a Sidonian, loved David and gave Solomon the materials and manpower to build the temple. These are our people, the goodly pleasant things, taken when we were in Africa. These weak men take every Israelite breakdown and say it is wrong: it is the same Christian doctrine, adapted.

“The children also of Judah and the children of Jerusalem have ye sold unto the Grecians, that ye might remove them far from their border.” The Arabs and the Hamites sold us to the Grecians, the so-called white man: the Dutch, the French, the Spanish, the Portuguese. These two were instrumental in our enslavement, and there are pictures of them selling us together, the Arab examining us and the Hamite pointing us out to the white man. They removed us far from our border, then moved in and parted the land, back to verse 2.

The Encyclopedia Americana co-signs it. It names the negroes, Bantu and Sudanic speaking, apart from the Hamites of the north and east, men of a physique differing from that of the negroes, with considerable crossbreeding between negroes and Hamites. How can the same race crossbreed? They are two different peoples. The Hamites pointed us out: that's not us, those are Israel over there. The Tuareg of the Sahara and the Somali are Hamites, the worst involved in our enslavement, and the ancient Egyptians were early Hamites. Semites, here the Arabs, like the Hamites have been a conquering race in Africa, both following the occupation of slave traders in negro territory until the end of the 19th century. They knew the difference. And under social conflicts: slavery was due to raids of Arabs and Hamites on negro communities. That is Joel 3 in the encyclopedia: Tyre and Zidon and the coasts of Palestine. Roots shows it too: Kunta in the forest sees the Hamite, the white man and the Arab working together, dragging our people away, removing us from our border.

precepts.why:
Nothing new. We had an evil king named Jehoram: “Jehoram was thirty and two years old when he began to reign, and he reigned eight years in Jerusalem.” “In his days the Edomites revolted from under the dominion of Judah, and made themselves a king”: because of him Edom gained authority. Libnah revolted too, “because he had forsaken the Lord God of his fathers.”

“Moreover the Lord stirred up against Jehoram the spirit of the Philistines, and of the Arabians, that were near the Ethiopians”. The Philistines: that is Tyre and Zidon, the Hamites. With them the Arabians, near the Ethiopians, the other Hamites. “And they came up into Judah, and brake into it”: into the negro community. They “carried away all the substance that was found in the king’s house, and his sons also, and his wives; so that there was never a son left him, save Jehoahaz, the youngest of his sons.” The Hamites and the Arabs got together and stole his wives and his children. It is their common nature: they steal people.

The records show it. The Arabs of Morocco, the northern neighbours of the negroes, were the first who purchased negro slaves, from the year 990, and brought Arabic, circumcision, the Quran and the rites of Muhammad among the black tribes beyond the Gambia; that is why Kunta Kinte came here a Muslim, his tribe conquered by the Muslims before the white man arrived. The Arabs and the Portuguese then competed over who could sell the most of us. Islamic law forbade Muslims to enslave each other, but they found black captives beyond the Sahara: nearly ten million from the 600s to the 1700s, in homes, fields and armies. The Arabs ran sugar plantations with us in Egypt and Syria for some three centuries; the Genoese, the Italians, copied the Arab model in the 1400s, and the Portuguese copied them on Madeira, the Canaries, Cape Verde and São Tomé, the island where they had thrown our children, and that plantation became the model for the Americas. The slaveholding of ancient Rome was not dead, and America is Rome again, the deadly wound healed. The Portuguese cut out the middleman and bought straight from the Hamite chieftains on the coast. At Timbuktu the people are real negroes, and the Arabs steal their girls and sell them for marriage; it is still slavery. The blacks disliked camels, because the camels are the beasts that carried them into slavery. Old accounts and the map of 1817 mark Yehudi, a place of great trade inhabited by one of the lost tribes of Israel, Yehuda meaning Judah, and Ouida as well: our kingdoms in Africa.

sense.text:
“And the Lord shall bring thee into Egypt again with ships”. Egypt is bondage, so the Lord would bring us into bondage again, this time by way of ships. “Thou shalt see it no more again”: you will never see literal Egypt again as a nation; this Egypt you reach by ships. “And there ye shall be sold unto your enemies for bondmen and bondwomen”: slave men and slave women. “And no man shall buy you”: no man shall save you.

Lest We Forget tells of the ships. The filth and stench, men packed so tight they could neither turn nor stand nor sit, for fifty days or more, for months, in spaces as tight as coffins: the Middle Passage, the Maafa, the great disaster. Tight packers and loose packers; most captains filled their ships to the top and added a second platform barely twenty inches above the heads of those below. Chained to the floor, lying in their own waste, menstrual blood and childbirth, rats gnawing through wood and flesh, the living waking chained to the dead. Horse beans pounded to a pulp, twice a day. At night the cries rose, because they had dreamt they were in their own country and woke in the hold of a slave ship. Those who say the slave ships are a myth because they cannot find them: before slaves, cargo ships carried spices and corn; then we were the cargo; when slavery was abolished, the same boats carried cargo again. Why get rid of them? That is jailhouse doctrine.

The Atlas of the Transatlantic Slave Trade says both buyers and sellers saw the people traded as outsiders: they knew who they were selling. Luanda, founded by the Portuguese in 1575, sent more captives to the Americas than any other port, most to Brazil. The old map marks Luanda Jews and Santo Jews, Gabon and Mayumba Jews, Kabinda survivals. The Loango coast and Angola coast sent about 45 percent of all the slaves to the Americas, and nearly 40 percent of the arrivals in South Carolina came from that region. Loango Bay was once called the Jews' Bay, Golfo de Judeu, on the old maps, because the Portuguese found the Jews there, natives with Jewish features, supposed to keep the Jewish Sabbath. Further south, by Ouidah, Whydah, the old writers called it Judah and its people Jews. The bulk of us went to South America; the small arrow to North America carried the princes, the sons of David and Jonathan and Aaron.

There is truth that we sold each other, but it is spun. We had kingdoms, and a kingdom divided against itself cannot stand: Israel fought itself, took war captives and sold them, and the white man armed one side then the other, conquered all of us, and put us all on the same ship. That is why those on the slave ships were the first to see that we were one people.

The Arabs had their own slave ships. The Nautical Magazine tells of the British, after they abolished slavery, intercepting the Arab dhows out of the Persian Gulf, the Arabs too lazy to do anything for themselves. At the Zanzibar market the slaves stood in rows, old men, old women, young men, young women, children, while the Arabs examined their eyes, teeth and tongues: casting lots, Joel 3 again. In the dhows they sat squeezed between the legs of the slave behind, fed millet and water, reduced to skeletons, covered in their own filth, and the smell carried a mile.

precepts.why: “I am the Lord thy God, which have brought thee out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of bondage.” What does Egypt represent? Bondage. So when the Lord says he will bring us “into Egypt again with ships”, he means into bondage again, by way of ships.

On the ships came the dancing of the slaves: the crew played the bagpipe or made our ancestors beat out a rhythm and jump about in their leg irons, to keep the human cargo in saleable condition. “For there they that carried us away captive required of us a song; and they that wasted us required of us mirth, saying, Sing us one of the songs of Zion.” We are reading it right there in the record. “How shall we sing the Lord’s song in a strange land?”

sense.text: “To sell her unto a strange nation he shall have no power, seeing he hath dealt deceitfully with her.” Why was that written? Because we were doing it. Israel, rebellious and stupid, was selling our own people off to the heathen for money, and God said you have no power to do that.
“And he that stealeth a man, and selleth him, or if he be found in his hand, he shall surely be put to death.” We were doing this, and it was death.

precepts.why: Now in Christ, if you were a trafficker you can repent. “The law is not made for a righteous man, but for the lawless and disobedient”, and the list includes “them that defile themselves with mankind”, homosexuals, and “menstealers”. That goes right back to Exodus 21:16, stealing people for slavery. If you are involved in child trafficking, get out of that nonsense.

sense.text:
The old histories say the Jews in Spain passed into Africa, to Mauritania and Numidia, as goldsmiths and blacksmiths, and that a town in Morocco was inhabited by Jews of the stock of David. When the king of Portugal put them out they went to Fez and Morocco and on to Timbuktu. And Egypt was ever near Palestine, as it were our second country. We always ran back and forth, Jerusalem to Egypt, Egypt to Jerusalem.

So: “Arise, and take the young child and his mother, and flee into Egypt, and be thou there until I bring thee word: for Herod will seek the young child to destroy him.” The angel told the black couple to flee into a black land from a white man.

“Then let them which are in Judea flee to the mountains”. Christ always said flee to the mountains, where you will be safe. The history of Africa says there is a populous nation of the Jewish stock west of the Nile under a mighty king, a province the cosmographers call the land of the Hebrews, between Abyssinia, Egypt and Congo, and mountain people of the Jews who keep themselves free in mountains that secure them from foreign nations and violent neighbours: the Arabs and the white man.
“For these be the days of vengeance, that all things which are written may be fulfilled.” And so we were scattered among the nations.

The records show who the Israelites are. Barbot says that at the close of the 15th century large numbers of Jews were expelled from Portugal and taken to the coast of southern Guinea, and that St. Thomas was peopled by mulattoes descended from the Jewish exiles, black men and white women. The missionaries at Loango regarded the people there as a pure African family of Jews. In Guinea the people keep circumcision, a division of the tribes into twelve families, the seven-day week, the new moons, bloody sacrifices, blood sprinkled on the doorposts and altars, a house of refuge to flee to, a distinct priesthood, rules of cleanliness and purification and mourning for the dead; and asked why, they answer, our fathers did it. Most of the negroes of America came from Guinea. These are Israelites, the black folks.

So “I know the blasphemy of them which say they are Jews, and are not, but are the synagogue of Satan.” That is the Israelis today, who stole our identity.

precepts.why: “Behold, I will make them of the synagogue of Satan, which say they are Jews, and are not, but do lie; behold, I will make them to come and worship before thy feet, and to know that I have loved thee.” They say they are Jews, but do lie. Now see who they are.

sense.text: “Son of man, set thy face against mount Seir, and prophesy against it”: against Edom. “Behold, O mount Seir, I am against thee, and I will stretch out mine hand against thee, and I will make thee most desolate.”
“Because thou hast had a perpetual hatred, and hast shed the blood of the children of Israel by the force of the sword in the time of their calamity”.

“I will make thee perpetual desolations”: Edom. “Because thou hast said, These two nations and these two countries shall be mine, and we will possess it”. In ancient times the two were Judah and Samaria, and the Greeks took over both; now the two nations are America and Israel.
“I will even do according to thine anger, and according to thine envy which thou hast used out of thy hatred against them; and I will make myself known among them, when I have judged thee.”

“I have heard all thy blasphemies which thou hast spoken against the mountains of Israel”. What blasphemy? Them which say they are Jews and are not, but do lie: saying that they are Judah, and that we are Christians. “Saying, They are laid desolate, they are given us to consume”: because we are desolate, they thought we were made for them to conquer.

Keep that in mind and read New World Jewry. The Jews, the so-called, were the largest ship chandlers in the whole Caribbean, where shipping was mainly a Jewish enterprise. The ships were owned by Jews, manned by Jewish crews and sailed under Jewish captains, and many were bringing slaves from Africa to the thirteen colonies, the British islands and the Spanish colonies. In Suriname plantations of sugar cane with hundreds of slaves were owned by Portuguese Jews; by 1730 the Jews owned 115 plantations out of 400. In 1782 the white population of Paramaribo was 2,000 souls, of whom 615 were Portuguese Jews and 430 German Jews: they counted themselves white then, and the Jews were a third to a half of the white population, merchant shippers. They were white then; now they are Jewish. Candace Owens posts it from the Jewish Encyclopedia: in the 17th century the sugar industry was monopolized by the Jews, and the cotton plantations in many parts of the south were wholly in their hands, so slavery found its advocates among them. The lists of slave ships and owners run Aaron Lopez, Moses Levy, Isaac Levy, Jacob Franks, Gomez, Cohen, the DeWolfs, and on and on. That is the blasphemy: the slave-ship owners now say they are Judah.

precepts.why: Who is mount Seir? “Thus dwelt Esau in mount Seir: Esau is Edom.” So when Ezekiel prophesies against mount Seir, he prophesies against Edom.

sense.text:
“The Lord shall smite thee with madness, and blindness, and astonishment of heart”. Once we came off those ships we were smitten with madness. Blindness means you cannot see: some of you watching still say Jesus and the Jews are white; you are gone. Astonishment of heart: you are just done, finished.

Twelve Years a Slave shows the madness. Patsey wakes Solomon Northup and begs him to take her to the swamp and hold her under the water until she has no life, because she is in madness: she had been beaten until her back was ripped open for a bar of soap, because she could not stand her own smell, and she says if he kills her it is a mercy, God will not hold him accountable. That is madness and trauma, and that is why reparations cannot fix this.

“And thou shalt grope at noonday, as the blind gropeth in darkness”: spiritual blindness. “Thou shalt not prosper in thy ways”: as a nation we do not prosper. “Thou shalt be only oppressed and spoiled evermore, and no man shall save thee.”

“Thou shalt betroth a wife, and another man shall lie with her”. We just watched it: in The Butler the white man takes the boy's mother out of the cotton field, cursed in the field, and rapes her, and her husband and son stand there powerless; all the father can do is be angry. In Birth of a Nation a guest demands Hark's wife Esther for the night right after they married, the master allows it, and she comes out in tears: where is God now? “Thou shalt build an house, and thou shalt not dwell therein: thou shalt plant a vineyard, and shalt not gather the grapes thereof.” We built it and did not dwell in it: want in the midst of plenty.

That is why there must be racial anger. Malcolm X, Martin Luther King and our people in the 50s, 60s and 70s knew who the enemy was, but after that we forgot and started saying our enemy is only a spiritual demon. They gave us Section 8, food stamps and Christianity, and we went back to sleep. So God put Trump in office: that administration will do a lot of evil to our people, and then you will realize this man is our enemy. The Lord is slowly reverting the white man to what he was before the 60s, to his true nature.

This is not new. “They ravished the women in Zion, and the maids in the cities of Judah.” They raped our women, our sisters, the women of Judah. Whatever colour the oppressor was, the nations all had the same habits, because judgment is like a ring: it comes around over and over again. Same game, different characters.

In Twelve Years a Slave the master preaches to his slaves from the Bible, that the servant which knew his lord's will and did not do it shall be beaten with many stripes, and tells them the lord in that verse is him, not Christ, and many means as many as he chooses: forty, a hundred, a hundred and fifty lashes. That is scripture, and we believed it. It is the same today: a white man says Jeremiah 14:2 is symbolic, you are eisegeting, and we fall for it.

“These things hast thou done, and I kept silence”: these things Esau did, and the Lord sat back and watched. I told you to keep my commandments and my laws, you said no, so I left you in the hands of your enemies and did nothing about it. “Thou thoughtest that I was altogether such an one as thyself”: when the white man conquered us he believed he was God, that our God was with him. You thought I was your God; I am not your God. “But I will reprove thee”: what you did was temporary, and I will correct you myself. “And set them in order before thine eyes”: he is setting us in order before their eyes, and it started in the 60s. That is why the revised Bibles came right after, the first in 1969: they knew the prophecies of the 350 years after Judah touched this soil, and changed the text before our children grew up. Now they push that they will no longer apologize, that slavery and the killing of the Native Americans are lies, taking the history out of the schools and the statues down. That is not for us; it is for our children, to take away their racial anger and their pride and give their own children a clear conscience. It is too late. You cannot stop it; it is already set in motion; our children will most likely see the Lord.

How does he reprove Edom? Wars, plagues and famine are coming on this earth, Russia and Ukraine, millions dead, the virus. While he judges them they are not paying attention to us, and his sons are waking up. If Esau were not busy with all that, his eyes would be on us.

That spark of resistance he tries to extinguish never left us: Nat Turner, Gabriel Prosser, Denmark Vesey, Medgar Evers, Dessalines, Toussaint Louverture, Geronimo, Atahualpa, Galvarino. In Roots Matilda tells the preacher she is a woman of faith, but not his faith: she is not interested in the white man's God. Kizzy says the only reason it is our faith is that it got beaten into us; let his God make slavery go away, and she will be in church every Sunday. No slave preacher could preach Exodus, the Israelites against Pharaoh: those pages were cut out of the slave Bible, and preaching it would leave you swinging from a low limb. The men who learned to read started revolutions, and what they read was the Bible, a book of insurrection. Jamaica made the book of Maccabees illegal. Almost every feast day, Passover, Tabernacles, Pentecost, Jubilee, Trumpets, is about liberation and freedom.

“Ye are the light of the world. A city that is set on an hill cannot be hid.” When you come into this truth you cannot hide. You start keeping the laws and commandments of God; you dress different, walk different, talk different, and you stand out. That is why they ask, where are you from? How was your Christmas? I don't celebrate that. How was your New Year? I took a nap. Thanksgiving, your birthday: it's a regular day. Where are you from? Esau, Ishmael and Moab ask it because they see that you are different, that spark, that light. It is the same as the mistress in Twelve Years a Slave asking Platt, where you from, who learned you to read? She knew he was no regular slave. Don't be too smart; that will earn you a hundred lashes. Because the men who learned to read revolted.

“Neither do men light a candle, and put it under a bushel, but on a candlestick; and it giveth light unto all that are in the house.” You come to this truth not to hide it but to bring forth the wisdom, the light, to the house of our people Israel.
“Let your light so shine before men, that they may see your good works”: your own people, that they may see your good works and take that light themselves and repent also.

precepts.why: “This is the book of the commandments of God, and the law that endureth for ever: all they that keep it shall come to life; but such as leave it shall die.” “Turn thee, O Jacob, and take hold of it”: of the book of commandments. “Walk in the presence of the light thereof”: the light is the commandments in that book. “That thou mayest be illuminated”: enlightened. Keeping the law makes you a light in a dark place that cannot be hid.

sense.text: “And thy life shall hang in doubt before thee”: you will wonder whether you will live or die. In the hood, the ghettos and the slums, and further back in slavery and colonization, it is the same: “thou shalt fear day and night, and shalt have none assurance of thy life”. Hanging in doubt does mean worry. But it also means hanging.
“In the morning thou shalt say, Would God it were even! and at even thou shalt say, Would God it were morning!” God, I hope I make it to tomorrow, “for the fear of thine heart”.

“Our inheritance is turned to strangers, our houses to aliens.” Our land is taken from us and we are colonized. The other nations are aliens: the European, the East Indian in Africa, the Chinese in East Africa and in Trinidad do not belong there, but they are there reaping and stealing the resources.
“We are orphans and fatherless, our mothers are as widows.” They killed our parents and our husbands.
“We have drunken our water for money; our wood is sold unto us.” Some of us in Africa and the Caribbean have to pay for our own water. That is colonization.
“Our necks are under persecution: we labour, and have no rest.”
“We have given the hand to the Egyptians”, the slave master, “and to the Assyrians, to be satisfied with bread.” Now we rely on our enemies for bread. These are the curses.
“Our fathers have sinned, and are not; and we have borne their iniquities.” Our fathers sinned and are dead, and we inherit the consequences of their actions.
“Servants have ruled over us”: those who were once our slaves now rule over us, “there is none that doth deliver us out of their hand.”
“We gat our bread with the peril of our lives because of the sword of the wilderness”: the sword of the wilderness is the oppressor.

“Princes are hanged up by their hand”: lynched. “The faces of elders were not honoured”: young or old, you were hung all the same. Without Sanctuary is a book of lynching photographs: our forefathers and foremothers hanging from trees, 1935, 1915, 1901, ninety years ago, yesterday. They were sold as postcards, and the crowds are families: fathers, mothers, children, the women right in the middle, the ones who grew up to be your lawyers, teachers, mayors and police officers. They burned the men and kept the pieces as souvenirs. They hanged a mother and son from a bridge. In 1918 Mary Turner, eight months pregnant, threatened to have the courts punish the men who lynched her husband; the next day they hung her from a tree, set her on fire, cut her abdomen open, and when the baby fell out crying a man crushed its head with his foot, and they shot her full of holes. And they say they will not apologize for that any more. Not long ago we could not use the same bathroom or ride the same bus, and in Queens in 1976 white crowds chased little black girls out of their neighbourhood with rocks. Those children are judges, lawyers and police officers now.

precepts.why: “Whosoever should transgress, yea, or make light of any thing afore spoken or written, out of his own house should a tree be taken, and he thereon be hanged, and all his goods seized for the king.” Hanging is nothing new. It has been around a long time, from the Persians to the Greeks and the Romans, always a punishment: in Persia the gallows were built for Mordecai, and the one who built them was hung on them instead.

“According to the commandment they put to death certain women, that had caused their children to be circumcised. And they hanged the infants about their necks”: after they killed the mothers, the Greeks hung their circumcised babies from their dead mothers' necks, up on display. They lynched our babies on their mothers' necks. “And rifled their houses, and slew them that had circumcised them”: Esau, so demonic and wicked, running around checking.

“We ought to obey God rather than men”: Peter told our wicked elders, God, not you. “The God of our fathers raised up Jesus, whom ye slew and hanged on a tree.” Christ was lynched. Peter called it hanging on a tree because the cross is made of wood.

Peter says it again: “whom they slew and hanged on a tree”. On wood. Some will say maybe he was hung from an actual tree. It is ironic: the same way the white man oppressed us, lynching us in slavery and in the 60s, is the way our king was killed.

Thomas says, “Except I shall see in his hands the print of the nails, and put my finger into the print of the nails, and thrust my hand into his side, I will not believe.” Why the nails? If he hung from an actual tree, what would they need nails for? He was nailed hands and feet to a cross and pierced in his side, and he hung there for hours, lynched slowly. Yet Peter called the cross a tree, wood.

They mocked him: “If thou be the Son of God, come down from the cross.” He was crucified, not hung by the neck from a tree; hanging by the neck he would have been choking to death and could not be answered. So when Peter says hung on a tree he means crucified. Christ was lynched, and the two men beside him were lynched also: capital punishment.

We did the same to the wicked: “if a man have committed a sin worthy of death, and he be to be put to death, and thou hang him on a tree: His body shall not remain all night upon the tree, but thou shalt in any wise bury him that day; (for he that is hanged is accursed of God;)”.

Hanging was our punishment too, for the wicked among us, and the one hanged on the tree is cursed.

“Christ hath redeemed us from the curse of the law”: from the condemnation of the law, a sacrifice, “being made a curse for us”, put to death for us, “for it is written, Cursed is every one that hangeth on a tree”. What happened to our people? We were hung on trees, because we are under the curses. Christ was under the curses of Deuteronomy 28 along with us. The king was hung, and his children were hung: it is the same exact thing.

sense.text: Moses and Aaron told Pharaoh, “Let my people go, that they may hold a feast unto me in the wilderness.” “And Pharaoh said, Who is the Lord, that I should obey his voice to let Israel go?”

“Wherefore do ye, Moses and Aaron, let the people from their works? get you unto your burdens.” Go back to work; I don't want to hear about your God. “The people of the land now are many, and ye make them rest from their burdens”: there are a whole bunch of you, and you want to stop working to go worship your God? No.

“Ye shall no more give the people straw to make brick, as heretofore: let them go and gather straw for themselves.” Yet the same tale of bricks, “for they be idle; therefore they cry, saying, Let us go and sacrifice to our God.” You are lazy; that is why you want to go sacrifice to your God. Black Americans worked hard as slaves and built this country, and today they call us lazy: it is the same thing.

“Let there more work be laid upon the men”. “Go ye, get you straw where ye can find it: yet not ought of your work shall be diminished.” He used to provide the straw; now that you want to be so lazy and serve your God, go find it yourself, and the task had better be done. “So the people were scattered abroad throughout all the land of Egypt to gather stubble instead of straw.”

“The officers of the children of Israel, which Pharaoh’s taskmasters had set over them, were beaten”. These officers are the black elites, the upper echelon the white man sets over us today: pastors, ministers, politicians, the black folks in the white man's pockets, like Jason Whitlock.

The officers cried to Pharaoh, “Wherefore dealest thou thus with thy servants?” Why are you beating us? And he said, “Ye are idle, ye are idle: therefore ye say, Let us go and do sacrifice to the Lord.” You want time off for your God because you are lazy. Go and work: “there shall no straw be given you, yet shall ye deliver the tale of bricks.”

The officers “did see that they were in evil case”. Pharaoh was a demon: he made the people turn on Moses and Aaron. “The Lord look upon you, and judge; because ye have made our savour to be abhorred in the eyes of Pharaoh, and in the eyes of his servants, to put a sword in their hand to slay us.” You made the white man hate us with your teaching and your Bible and your God; now we have to work harder; you are spreading hate, being militant, you are going to get us locked up and killed. That is you who stood quiet in the back.

Moses said, “Lord, wherefore hast thou so evil entreated this people? why is it that thou hast sent me?” Why send me to them, when they hate me more now? But the Most High had his own plan.

Nothing new under the sun; judgment is a ring. In Twelve Years a Slave Epps weighs the cotton each slave picked against the quota: two hundred pounds for an average slave, and Patsey picked five hundred, through the thorns. We had a quota in Egypt too. A leather scroll from the fifth year of Ramesses II lists forty stable masters, each with a target of 2,000 bricks, and Yupa son of Urhiya, a Hebrew name, delivered 1,630, a deficit of 370. The text echoes Pharaoh stopping the straw and still demanding the full quota, and other texts show Egyptian workers given days off for their own religious holidays. The Egyptians got their days off for their gods; when we asked for ours, we were called lazy and idle.

We are still slaves today. They give you their pagan holidays off, Christmas and New Year's, two weeks' vacation, five sick days; use too many and they put you on sick leave and watch you. At the transit job they did not call you by your name, only your pass number, and when a booth clerk dropped dead they moved his body over and kept selling the cards. They are paying you for your time, and your time is your life. That is why they call you a civil servant: you are a servant.

“The fruit of thy land, and all thy labours, shall a nation which thou knowest not eat up; and thou shalt be only oppressed and crushed alway”. That is the oppression the man in the slave ship was told he would face on this side of the world: in American Gods the spider god of Africa tells the captives that the moment the Dutch set foot there they decided they were white and you get to be black; you will be slaves, sold off and worked to death, a hundred years later still getting screwed out of jobs and shot by police. That is what the prophets told us, what Moses told us, and we did not believe it. We laughed.

“So that thou shalt be mad for the sight of thine eyes which thou shalt see.” That is racial anger in the scriptures. Your eyes will be mad for the oppression you see: your people oppressed, your wife raped and you can do nothing, your people lynched and you can do nothing. If you see your people going through these things and you are not mad, not angry, something is not right: you have shut down. There must be racial anger.
